description: S458 2a-fix F2: a block-bodied arrow (or function expression) is opaque to the type stage — the compiler keeps its body as text — so no check can be placed inside it. A write it makes into an OUTER refined local (`k = @m` with `k: number(>0)`) would ship unchecked; it is refused at compile time with E-CONTRACT-002 instead. (A write into a reactive cell from the same arrow is fine: the runtime setter judges it.)
rationale: §53.11 E-CONTRACT-001-RT: "The compiler SHALL emit a runtime check for every boundary-zone assignment that it cannot statically elide." A write the compiler cannot place a check on is refused rather than admitted unchecked (the E-CONTRACT-002 "cannot be judged" sense, §53.11: "its runtime check SHALL NOT admit values it cannot judge").
